facts.text: The package controls the Nikon Ti2-E microscope over the reverse-engineered USB protocol through PyUSB, without the Nikon SDK
MicroscopeDevice is constructed from a usb.core.Device and owns the asyncio lock its commands share
StatusEvent reports the condenser (0-6), filter (0-5), objective (0-5), optical path (0-3), diaphragm opening (0-1), light, shutter, x and y [0.1 um], z [0.01 um] and the zoom code
set_condenser accepts an index from 0 to 6
set_dia accepts a diaphragm opening from 0.0 to 1.0
set_filter accepts an index from 0 to 5
set_objective accepts an index from 0 to 5
set_optical_path accepts an index from 0 to 3
set_x and set_y send a signed 32-bit position in 0.1 um and set_z sends one in 0.01 um
The x and y stage bounds and the z stage bound are queried from the device at run time; the clone states no fixed travel
get_status returns the next StatusEvent and get_stable_status returns the last one once no newer event arrives within idle_duration (0.5 s by default)
get_firmware_cpu_version returns five ASCII bytes as the CPU version
set_light and set_shutter take a boolean that enables or disables the light and the shutter
On macOS and Linux a firmware bug makes get_event and other status calls return with a minimum delay of 4.096 s, and queued events may not be up to date
